The Problem
36 million businesses in America need insurance—it's not optional. 77% are underinsured. 40% have no coverage at all. The distribution system failed them: too slow, too opaque, too confusing.
Over 90% of commercial insurance is still human-led. We're building the inverse: 90%+ AI-led, pushing toward the higher 90s. Not by patching legacy workflows—by building AI that makes humans more effective, improves the customer experience, and eliminates friction at every step.
We're adding ~1,000 customers per month. We've grown 100x since last year. We're looking to do even more this year—and that's why we're hiring.
You'll build the team and the systems the rest of engineering depends on. When they compound, everyone gets faster.
The Thesis
Harper runs 200+ services across Railway and AWS. We orchestrate N parallel agentic workloads. Our AI systems make thousands of decisions a day, and every decision needs to be traceable, evaluated, and cheaper to run tomorrow than it is today. The infrastructure underneath all of that is the difference between a company that scales and one that stalls.
Great platform engineering here isn't invisible—it's the reason product ships fast. When observability catches a silent failure before a customer does. When a pooling layer makes connection exhaustion a non-issue. When developer velocity doubles because someone built the tool nobody knew they needed. That leverage compounds across every other engineer on the team.

This role is open both to an experienced EM and to someone on the path to becoming an EM who doesn't yet have significant management experience—we're happy to bring that person on and support the transition.
This is a team that still needs to be built. We have 2 people in it today, and we believe this area needs significant investment at Harper.

The role owns three things: infrastructure (cloud, third-party vendors, and everything surrounding it), developer productivity (making sure we're genuinely an AI-first shop, with the right AI tooling and harnesses in place for every other engineering team to be successful), and SRE and production support (production discipline is top of mind as we head into a high-growth, high-scale phase—we need someone who has run an SRE function before).

Each of these three areas can grow into a larger team of its own over time.
The team is 2 people today, growing to five to six over the next three months. Because the team is small, whoever takes this role—EM or TLM—will need to be hands-on at the start, working directly with the team and doing the work themselves.

Who We Are
DoiT is a global technology company that works with cloud-driven organizations to leverage the cloud to drive business growth and innovation. We combine data, technology, and human expertise to ensure our customers operate in a well-architected and scalable state - from planning to production.
Delivering DoiT Cloud Intelligence, the only solution that integrates advanced technology with human intelligence, we help our customers solve complex multicloud problems and drive efficiency.
With decades of multicloud experience, we have specializations in Kubernetes, GenAI, CloudOps, and more. An award-winning strategic partner of AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, we work alongside more than 4,000 customers worldwide.
The Opportunity
The Engineering Manager is a hands-on, player-coach leadership role. You are embedded with your team - daily standup, code review, architectural calls, delivery planning, and performance management - and you own both the team's output and the team's growth.
This is a genuinely technical & leadership role. You are expected to write and review code, be a credible voice in architectural decisions, and stay current in your team's stack. You lead by demonstrating you can do the work at the highest level, not by title alone.
The balance between hands-on contribution and leadership depends on the team's context, but your overarching mandate is the same: run the team, execute and deliver, and grow its impact.
Build the bench, raise the standard, and keep the operating cadence sharp as the work and the organization evolve. You work AI-augmented yourself, expect the same from your team, and push the team's craft forward with every new capability that lands.

Team leadership & growth
Leading a team of engineers, owning both its delivery and its development.
Lead a mindset and process of continuous improvement within the team and meaningfully impact the team’s growth and success over time. Small, compounding improvements, delivered via fast iterations, are the operating rhythm we expect, not an aspiration.
You are responsible for the professional well-being and career development of team members. Develop engineers through regular 1:1s, growth plans, performance reviews, and direct, candid feedback.
Develop the next layer of leadership - tech leads, senior engineers ready to manage, and ICs ready to step into staff roles.
Technical leadership
Write code and review code. Be a credible voice in technical decisions because you have hands in the work, not because of your title - you are current, not rusty.
Drive the team's architectural and technical design decisions in partnership with senior ICs, ensuring alignment on approach and implementation.
Uphold engineering standards through thorough, constructive pull-request review and a healthy release process, keeping the team's components scalable and in a healthy state.
Work AI-augmented and lead an AI-augmented team, applying sharp judgment about where AI helps and holding the same quality bar for what ships.
Roadmap & delivery
Own the team's commitments - what was promised, when it was promised, and the quality bar that was held.
Run a disciplined cadence of planning, prioritization, and delivery without becoming a process bureaucrat.

General Description
Crane Worldwide Logistics ships freight across the globe. The Software Integrations group builds the software that connects the systems that make that happen. We are seeking an Engineering Manager to found our Corporate Integrations team.

You will hire its engineers, establish its practices, and build its relationships with stakeholders across the business. This team will own integrations for the corporate systems that support our logistics business, such as finance, billing, and procurement.

In practice that means moving data between systems and building APIs to provide a clean access layer to those systems for other engineering teams within Crane. This is primarily a leadership role, with hands-on contribution expected early as the team forms. This is the first role on a new team, which you will grow to three engineers.

Our business stakeholders know their processes deeply, and a core part of this role is turning that knowledge into buildable integration designs and APIs. Your team owns and shapes its backlog, and the roadmap is driven in close partnership with the business. Our software is built in F# on AWS.

Deep C# or other .NET experience with a willingness to lead a functional-programming team is welcome. Prior functional programming experience is a plus. This is a fully remote position within the United States and reports to the Director of Software Integrations.
Essential Job Functions
Build the Corporate Integrations team from the ground up by recruiting and hiring three engineers.
Lead, mentor, and manage the team day to day, ensuring high performance and professional growth.
Work directly with business stakeholders to elicit and document requirements, translating process descriptions into well-scoped integration designs.
Own and prioritize the team's backlog in partnership with business stakeholders who drive the roadmap.
Oversee the software development lifecycle for the team's integrations and APIs, from requirements through deployment and maintenance.
Drive engineering best practices as part of a maturing engineering organization, including automated testing, CI/CD, code reviews, design reviews, monitoring, and observability.
Ensure the security, scalability, and reliability of the team's integrations and APIs through effective architecture and coding practices.
Contribute code and technical direction as needed, particularly in the team's early stages.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams and engineering leadership to align with organization-wide standards.

Required
Bachelor of Science in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
7+ years of experience in software development, with at least 3 years in a managerial or leadership role.
Deep expertise within the .NET ecosystem. Our systems are written in F#, and leaders with a strong C# background who are eager to lead a functional[1]programming team are welcome.
Solid working knowledge of a major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP)
Strong understanding of relational databases and distributed systems
Comfort with ambiguity and a demonstrated ability to work with non[1]technical stakeholders to discover, clarify, and document requirements
Strong communication, leadership, and interpersonal skills
Ability to manage multiple projects and prioritize effectively
Must be eligible to work in the United States on an ongoing basis without sponsorship

AWS experience specifically (we use ECS, Aurora, and related services)

Prior experience building a team from scratch
Experience at an early-stage startup, or standing up a new team inside a larger company

SeatGeek believes live events are powerful experiences that unite humans. With our technological savvy and fan-first attitude we’re simplifying and modernizing the ticketing industry.
Reporting to the VP of Engineering, the Director of Engineering will lead the engineering organization responsible for the systems at the core of how teams, venues, and promoters manage tickets and operate their businesses. Hundreds of major live event venues around the globe rely on the SeatGeek platform, including those home to the Dallas Cowboys, Cleveland Cavaliers, Florida Panthers, and Manchester United F.C.
You will set technical direction for this complex, mature platform while helping lead its evolution toward SeatGeek’s next generation of products and architecture. At the same time, you will help change how we build software as we move toward an AI-native engineering organization.
This role requires someone who can move comfortably between technology, product, and the ticketing domain. You will partner closely with Product and Design leadership, Engineering Managers, Senior Engineers, and our clients to turn complicated business problems into clear technical and product direction.

Set technical direction across US Ticketing, working with Engineering Managers and Staff+ engineers on architecture, system ownership, modernization, and platform boundaries
Lead the evolution of a mature, business-critical platform, balancing client commitments and near-term delivery with long-term reliability, scalability, and modernization
Stay close to the technology and contribute directly when useful, whether through code, prototypes, debugging, architecture reviews, technical designs, or documentation
Pioneering AI-native engineering by evolving how teams design, build, test, operate, and understand software, and by turning successful experiments into repeatable improvements
Partner as a peer with Product and Design leadership to shape strategy, not simply execute a roadmap
Develop a deep understanding of our clients and business, distinguish client-specific needs from durable platform opportunities, and participate directly in important client, sales, and implementation conversations when engineering context matters
Lead and develop Engineering Managers and senior technical leaders, creating clear ownership and strong leverage through others
Build a strong engineering organization by developing leaders, growing Staff+ talent, and evolving team structure as the business changes
Create an engineering culture that combines high ownership, healthy technical debate, strong execution, and sustainable performance
What you have
Experience leading multiple engineering teams and Engineering Managers in a complex software organization
Strong technical judgment and enough architectural depth to work credibly with senior engineers on difficult system and platform decisions
A willingness and ability to contribute technically when it is the highest-leverage way to help, including architecture, technical writing, prototyping, debugging, and code
Hands-on experience with AI-assisted software development and a strong point of view on how AI changes engineering practices and the software development lifecycle
Experience evolving mature, business-critical systems while continuing to deliver customer value
A track record of creating technical strategy from ambiguous product and business problems
Experience partnering closely with senior Product and Design leaders and learning complex customer domains quickly
Experience developing Engineering Managers and Staff+ engineers and creating leverage through other leaders
Strong cross-functional leadership, communication, ownership, and comfort making consequential decisions with incomplete information
Experience with ticketing, live events, commerce, payments, reservations, inventory, or similarly complex transactional systems is a plus
Our stack
US Ticketing includes mature systems that have powered some of the world’s largest live events for years alongside newer services and applications. We care much more about your ability to understand complex systems, make sound architectural decisions, lead modernization, and use new tools effectively than experience with any particular language or framework.
This is a deeply technical leadership role. We do not expect the Director to be the primary implementer, but we do expect them to be willing and able to contribute technically when it helps move the team forward. AI is becoming a core part of our engineering process, and this leader will help us rethink how teams build and evolve software in an AI-native development environment.

Unzer is a leading European fintech company with a mission to simplify international payments for e-commerce and retail businesses. Our brand was formed from 13 companies that now contribute to building a unique product covering the entire payment flow.
At Unzer, we are driven by the belief that customers should enjoy a seamless shopping experience, no matter where they choose to shop. We are a team of over 750 experts from 70 different nationalities, dedicated to creating a state-of-the-art unified commerce platform. Our goal is to enable businesses to delight their customers with a seamless payment experience.
Whether you're a tech enthusiast, payment expert, or a dedicated support professional, we are looking for individuals who are passionate about making a difference.
Our offices: We are based across Austria, Denmark, Germany, and Luxembourg, with our HQ in Berlin.

Our Payment Processing team owns the core of Unzer's platform — the systems that authorise, capture and settle every merchant transaction, at high volume and under strict reliability and compliance demands. We're also building AI into both our tooling and our payment flows. The team is cross-functional and owns its services end to end; as Engineering Manager, you'll lead experienced engineers and work closely with Product, Risk and Operations.

s.h: What your work will look like
s.t:
Leads, mentors, and grows a team of engineers, owning hiring, performance management, and career development.
Remains hands-on when needed, contributing to the codebase, troubleshooting complex issues, and supporting the team with your technical expertise.
Takes accountability for the delivery, quality, and reliability of one or more product areas, balancing technical and business priorities.
Partners with product and other stakeholders to shape roadmaps, plan capacity, and ensure predictable delivery.
Drives continuous improvement of engineering practices, tooling, and processes, and removes blockers for the team.
Contributes to technical and architectural direction, ensuring sound decisions while empowering engineers to own the details.

s.h: What you need to be successful in this role
s.t:
Bachelor's or  Master's degree in Computer Science  or similar, with substantial software engineering experience and prior people-management or tech-lead experience.
Proven ability to lead, coach, and develop engineers, and to build inclusive, motivated teams.
Strong technical grounding (e.g., Java, Kotlin, and/or JavaScript, large-scale systems) sufficient to guide architecture and challenge decisions—without needing to be the hands-on expert.
Familiarity with Agentic Software Engineering and AI-driven development lifecycles, and how to adopt them within a team.
Deep understanding of Agile delivery, CI/CD, and quality practices, plus excellent communication and stakeholder-management skills across teams and functions.
Experience with cloud-based, containerized environments (Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS) is a plus.
Fluent in English, with excellent communication and stakeholder-management skills.
Please note that we will not sponsor your visa or relocation, and you must have a valid work permit to be eligible for this position.
What’s next?
Does it sound exciting? - Apply with your CV in English. Please don’t shy away if you don’t meet all the requirements! We’re looking forward to meeting you.
The interview process includes: a 30min intro call with a TA Partner, a 60-min Hiring Manager interview, a take-home assignment optional), a 60-min skills assessment call with the team, and a 30-min executive interview, 30 min.
